sections.skill: Make visuals accessible with alt text, contrast and labels

questions.prompt: What is alt text?

choices.text: A short description so screen readers can read an image aloud
The file name of the image, such as "photo123.jpg,"

questions.correct_answer: A short description so screen readers can read an image aloud
questions.intro: ACCESSIBLE visuals work for more people, including people who are blind or have low vision, color blindness or reading difficulties. ALT TEXT is a short written description attached to an image so screen readers can read it aloud: it says what matters in the image for its purpose ("Bar chart: sales doubled from March to June"), not "image.jpg." CONTRAST means text stands out clearly from its background, such as dark text on a light background. CLEAR LABELS put words on chart lines and parts instead of relying on color alone. AI can draft alt text, but you check it.

sections.skill: Compare alt text with describing a picture over the phone

questions.prompt: Saying "It's a file called IMG_204" is like what?
questions.correct_answer: Useless alt text
questions.intro: Imagine calling a friend and describing a photo they cannot see. You would not say "It's a file called IMG_204." You would say what matters: "It's our team holding the trophy after winning the final." You skip unimportant details like the exact color of the wall. Alt text works the same way: a short spoken-style description of what matters in the image, for someone who cannot see it.

sections.skill: Fix weak alt text and color-only signals

questions.prompt: Generated alt text for a chart says "colorful shapes." What is missing?

choices.text: More colors, since describing the colors fully is the most important part of chart alt text

questions.correct_answer: The data or key finding
questions.intro: Generated alt text can be wrong or miss the point: it might describe a chart as "colorful shapes" without the data, or guess at things that are not there. Alt text should match the image's purpose; a decorative border may need none, while an important chart needs its key finding. Color-only signals, such as "red means late," fail for many viewers, so add words or symbols. Some screen readers can recognize text inside images, but not reliably, so give important text as real text or alt text.
